assets.alt: Flying DNA presentation workflow links drone sensing, wind sensing, city-model registration, urban wind fields, wind prediction, and wind effects on a drone.
assets.description: The workflow begins on the left with a wind-sensor image and an outdoor drone image. Arrows connect the drone to a Drone Sensing Network illustration and to Wind Impact on Drone. Along the top, Drone Sensing Network points to Wind Sensing, then to City Model Registration. A vertical connection labelled CFD/Physics-Informed AI leads from the city model to an Urban Wind Field rendering. The bottom row connects Urban Wind Field to Wind Prediction and then to Wind Impact on Drone, returning toward the drone. Written labels and this sequence identify the components without requiring the viewer to distinguish arrow colors. This is a conceptual overview from the broader presentation, not a verified deployment report or the exact modified-PPO architecture used in the 2025 eVTOL article.

video.full_visual_description: A silent, 20.93-second urban flight simulation taken from slide 6 of the Flying DNA presentation. A small four-rotor aircraft is shown above streets and intersections between multistory buildings. The rendered city includes cars, crosswalks, sidewalks, and reflective road surfaces. A broad yellow path or trail meets the aircraft and curves through the scene. The camera follows the aircraft from changing rear, elevated, and side viewpoints, first overlooking a street and an intersection, then moving closer to a building facade. The final view shows the aircraft beside the buildings with the yellow trace extending across the image. The complete original animation is retained at its original timing and resolution, without cropping, added motion, or audio. This is a drone simulation from the broader presentation; it does not by itself establish the aircraft model, controller, wind condition, quantitative performance, or identity of the city, and it is not footage of the 2025 eVTOL policy operating on a real aircraft.
